definition: Setting monthly and plan cost allocation percentages, distributing cost center and labor reports, and getting misposted charges corrected.

synthesis.description: Operations accounting sets the allocation of Texas Operations costs across cost centers, both for the annual plan and month by month. Brenda Herod sends allocation files and asks managers to review them and update the spreadsheet with changes; Lisa Cousino sets up responsibility centers (RCs), announces charges that will or will not appear, and asks staff to check their RC reports for misposted charges. Labor Distribution and budget-versus-actual reports are distributed, and staff flag people or charges showing in the wrong place so they can be corrected.
steps: Accounting prepares the plan or monthly allocation file for Texas Operations.
The allocation is sent to managers, who review it and return changes.
The allocation spreadsheet is updated and the final allocation is issued.
Monthly RC, Labor Distribution and budget-versus-actual reports are distributed.
Staff check their RC and labor reports for misposted charges or employees.
Misposted charges are reported and corrected with the RC owner or corporate.
synthesis.approach: Keep the allocation percentages in one shared, structured workbook with a fixed layout per cost center, and generate a monthly exception report that compares RC postings against the allocation and the employee roster, flagging misposted charges and people showing in the wrong RC for owners to confirm.
synthesis.rationale: Most rework comes from editing ad hoc spreadsheets and from owners eyeballing RC reports for errors. A standard allocation template removes the broken-spreadsheet step and gives reviewers a consistent sheet to mark up, while an exception check narrows manual review to the flagged lines.
